title: What do we get when we multiply triangular numbers by six and add one?
description: Each triangular number is multiplied by six, and then one is added. The results are seven, nineteen, thirty seven, sixty one and ninety one, and a picture of six triangles around a centre dot shows why.
teaching_notes: One idea: six triangles of dots around one centre dot make a hexagon of dots. Watch for students who add one before multiplying by six.

source: Figure it Out Q7 (Try This), p.9
video_script.why: The child builds a new sequence from the triangular numbers by a fixed rule and uses a picture of dots to see which sequence it is.
video_script.substitution: The rule is times six, plus one, applied to the triangular numbers.
video_script.anchor: a centre dot with six triangles of dots around it
video_script.payoff_line: Six times a triangular number plus one gives the hexagonal numbers, with six triangles around a centre dot
maths_rules: six triangles of 3 dots around a centre dot is 6 x 3 + 1 = 19 dots
the book's hexagonal numbers are 1, 7, 19, 37, ..., and these results are the ones after the first, 1
video_script.design: The triangular numbers are drawn as triangles of dots. Six copies are placed round a centre dot, and the dots are counted.
